items.title: China Energy Engineering wins offshore wind EPC contract
points: China Energy Engineering’s Guangdong Electric Power Design Institute has won an engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract to deliver offshore electrical infrastructure for two wind farms totalling 800MW off China’s Guangdong province.
The award, confirmed by National Energy Group, covers the Jiangmen Chuandao I and II offshore wind developments, each with a planned capacity of 400MW.
The Chinese contractor submitted a bid of RMB1.0267bn ($144m), according to an earlier tender announcement.
The final contract value has not been separately disclosed.

The scope includes engineering and design work, equipment procurement, fabrication, transportation, offshore installation, and commissioning of a 500kV offshore booster station and a reactive-power compensation station.
The two wind farms are located approximately 62 km and 68 km offshore Jiangmen, with Chuandao II occupying waters between 39 and 45 metres deep.
The turbines will collect power through 66kV subsea cables and transmit it to the offshore booster station, where the voltage will be increased to 500kV.

items.title: Maersk boxship knocks down crane at Yantian
points: A Maersk-operated containership has brought down a ship-to-shore crane at China’s Yantian port after striking the structure while berthing.
The incident involved the 366-m-long, 15,516 teu Maersk Cincinnati, which hit the crane at berth 12 of the Shenzhen terminal at around noon local time on November 9.
Images and videos shared across Chinese social media show the crane collapsed towards the container yard, with sections of the structure lying alongside the vessel.
The Singapore-flagged, 2024-built boxship was operating voyage 645W on the Gemini Cooperation’s Asia-North Europe NE3 service.
AIS data placed the vessel at Yantian on Monday, with the ship still alongside on Tuesday.
It had been scheduled to depart on November 11 for Ningbo and Shanghai before heading to Tanjung Pelepas in Malaysia and onward to Europe.
Shenzhen’s meteorological authorities issued a monsoon warning at 6.10 am on Monday for Yantian and surrounding waters, with gusts of force 8 or above forecast.

items.title: Andhra teachers’ associations flag anomalies in new service rules
points: The associations said they had repeatedly requested the government to frame comprehensive and uniform service rules for Government and Panchayat Raj teachers in the wake of the Presidential Order, 2025.

Leaders of the associations said the new rules did not comprehensively cover all categories of Gazetted Headmasters and lacked clarity on the classification of certain posts and their methods of appointment, including promotion and appointment by transfer.

They also pointed out that the relationship between the earlier service rules issued in 1998, the 2017 rules and the newly notified provisions had not been clearly explained, potentially creating confusion over their applicability and continuity.
The associations sought clarification on the separate service rules issued for Government and Zilla Parishad Gazetted Headmasters under G.O.

They also questioned the classification of Gazetted Headmasters, Mandal Educational Officers (MEOs) and DIET lecturers into different service categories despite their respective supervisory, administrative and academic responsibilities.

items.title: Oxford University returns remains of 39 Naga people after more than a century
points: Dimapur/Kohima, The University of Oxford returned the remains of 39 members of the Naga community, which were held at its Pitt Rivers Museum for more than a century, in a historic repatriation initiative.
The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on Monday.
The transfer of title document was signed by Pitt Rivers Museum Director Professor Laura Van Broekhoven and FNR representative Rev Dr Wati Aier.
It was witnessed by Visier Sanyu on behalf of the FNR and Thejao Vihienuo representing the Naga Tribe Hoho.
Following the handover, the ancestral remains were moved from the University of Oxford to begin their journey to Nagaland, according to a statement issued by the FNR on Tuesday.
The remains had been part of the collections of the Pitt Rivers Museum, established in 1884, which houses cultural artefacts collected from different parts of the world.

items.title: India's Race To The Bottom Of The Ocean: What Lies 6,000 Metres Below?

The vehicle is designed to take three aquanauts - people trained to work underwater - to depths of up to 6,000 metres.

That earlier order marked DHT’s return to Hanwha following the completion of its initial two-vessel programme at the South Korean shipbuilder.
The latest deal leaves DHT with two VLCCs on order at Hanwha, extending its fleet renewal programme into 2029.
DHT reported average spot earnings of $167,100 per day during the third quarter, while its vessels on time charter earned an average of $114,200 per day.

items.title: Why Rocket Lab shares fell despite record revenue and booming Neutron demand
points: Rocket Lab shares fell more than 6% in after-hours trading on November 9 after the space company reported a wider-than-expected quarterly loss.
(Sources: Asianet Newsable, TradingKey) Rocket Lab reported third-quarter revenue of $267.83 million, up 73% from a year earlier and above analysts' estimates of around $257 million.
Rocket Lab's backlog increased 52% sequentially to approximately $3.57 billion at the end of the September quarter.
The company expects around $1.17 billion of this amount to convert into revenue over the next 12 months, providing visibility into future business.
Rocket Lab secured more than $515 million in Neutron launch contracts during the quarter, covering eight missions.
The company raised the rocket's base launch price to $70 million from $55 million for several missions, reflecting strong demand and tightening launch capacity.
Rocket Lab expects fourth-quarter revenue of $270 million to $290 million, above analysts' expectations of approximately $265 million.
Rocket Lab received a conditional $150 million loan commitment from the Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital.

points: Sonia Gandhi reveals in her memoir that she has had minimal contact with PM Narendra Modi.
Their encounters are restricted to formal greetings at political gatherings, often avoiding eye contact.
Gandhi contrasts her vision of an inclusive India with Modi's more exclusionary ideology shaped by the RSS.

items.title: 'Should've called it Whitewashing, not Belonging': BJP mocks Sonia Gandhi's memoir
points: BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan criticized Sonia Gandhi's memoir, arguing it attempts to whitewash the historical mistakes of the Congress party.
He highlighted her emotional responses to key incidents while questioning her silence on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and other tragedies.
The memoir details Sonia's childhood, her marriage to Rajiv Gandhi, and her experiences as part of the Gandhi family.

DIAL rains for relief: Choked Delhi to see another cloud seeding attempt
points: India’s capital, New Delhi, will attempt cloud seeding to induce rain and address severe pollution.
The initiative involves Delhi International Airport Ltd, the Delhi government, and IIT Kanpur.
A specialized aircraft from Kyathi Climate will undertake the operation on Tuesday and Wednesday.
A fresh western disturbance is expected to bring rain to northwestern India later this week.
Cloud seeding aims to enhance precipitation as the air quality deteriorates.

items.title: 'Warrants urgent attention': SC flags vehicular pollution in Delhi-NCR, seeks action plan
points: The Supreme Court has mandated that Delhi and three adjacent states intensify measures to combat vehicle emissions.
Officials are tasked with reporting on the implementation of laws governing aging and non-compliant vehicles.
With rising pollution levels in the National Capital Region, the court emphasized the need for inter-state collaboration on vehicle management and stricter adherence to emission standards.
The matter will be reviewed again on November 23.
